summary.intent: Land two ordered structural PRs in the callisto repo: (1) introduce a ConvergedTargets type so only the cascade solver's final step can supply targets to range rewrites and E319 checks, (2) move dependency-range rewriting into the Versioning trait. Both were to follow AGENTS.md's invariant ladder and the lead's gating rules.
summary.outcome: PR #594 (ConvergedTargets, behaviour-preserving, no changeset) was pushed at de10f438 with all 16 CI checks green and no Entire findings. PR 2 was dropped by the lead before any code was written because of the MIT/FSL license split and because #573 already fixed the epoch bug.

repo: Cascade targets were only correct because cascade.rs ran steps in order; ConvergedTargets::settle now makes the final solver step the only way to build the type that rewrite_edge/rewrite_spec accept.

Rust cannot narrow visibility to a sibling module (pub(in crate::commands::snapshot) is not allowed on an item in cascade). The fix was to move snapshot's rewrite loop into cascade so the constructor stays pub(super).

apply.rs makes no coverage, rewrite or E319 decisions; it writes already-computed PlannedBump.to and SpecRewrite.to. Gating it would need a test-util feature for integration tests that build plans directly, which invariant 6 forbids.

The Versioning trait lives in callisto-model (MIT) while the rewrite code lives in callisto-manifests (FSL), so moving rewriting into the trait would relicense code. Cargo and npm rewrites also differ despite sharing SemVer.
docs/architecture/versioning.md documents the cascade steps and needed a bullet for the new type; doc-check fails on intra-doc links to now-private items such as rewrite_spec.

Running cargo-mutants on the diff surfaced an untested behaviour (the peer-escalation changelog entry); a new test in commands/version/tests.rs closed it, giving 34 mutants with 19 caught, 15 unviable and 0 missed.

code.finding: New ConvergedTargets/ConvergedTarget types. The reviewer recommended dropping the Deref and Index impls and keeping version() and get(), and tightening the doc comments that overclaimed.

solve_cascade keeps a local provisional BTreeMap and calls ConvergedTargets::settle once the worklist converges. out.targets is empty during the loop, so later code in raise() reading out.targets would silently get None. rewrite_spec was made pub(crate) because its signature changed.

The snapshot rewrite loop was moved into cascade (snapshot_rewrites). snapshot_versions is still cloned because platform_version_writes uses it afterwards; moving that call earlier would change which error surfaces first.

workflow: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5: 18 cores gives 3, taken from getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN because sysctl output was empty.
cargo mutants --in-place mutates the working tree, so edits must not run concurrently with it. It also leaves untracked proptest-regressions files that must be deleted before committing.

The sandbox blocks the npm cache (~/.npm/_cacache) and the gpg keyring, so just test and signed commits had to run outside it. Local signature checks fail in the sandbox, so verification was done via the GitHub API.
entire trail ci-pr creates the PR with a placeholder title and body, so it was then edited with gh pr edit while keeping Entire's marker.

The lead relaxed the gating mid-task (only cargo test -p, just lint, just doc-check; no local just ci, no reviewer, no mutants for behaviour-preserving refactors), so work had to adapt to changed rules.
Raising design and license concerns before writing code saved a whole PR's worth of effort.

friction: Sandbox restrictions on the npm cache and gpg keyring forced re-runs of the test gate and the commit outside the sandbox.
The mutation run takes about 10 minutes and blocks edits in the same worktree, and it ran twice because the review changes and new test invalidated the first run.
The lead's mid-task rule change cancelled a running just ci and made earlier review and mutant work partly redundant.
Dropping Deref and Index required edits across many test call sites and several scratch python edit scripts.
doc-check broke on an intra-doc link to rewrite_spec after it became private.
open_items: Reviewer's optional suggestion, not done: build CascadeOutcome after settle instead of threading out through the solver loop, so out.targets is never an empty default during solving.
PR 2 (moving range rewriting into the Versioning trait so each grammar owns bump and rewrite) was dropped; no change was made to the free-function rewrites in python.rs, npm and cargo.
Apply remains plain data and is not gated by ConvergedTargets, by decision.
The graph crate changelog question for the rewrite_spec visibility change was not explicitly resolved.
